sentences.label: Lowering the risk
sentences.text: These add up independently, and these lower the risk: being a woman takes a typical patient's predicted risk from about 18% to about 2%, typical angina to about 2%, non-anginal chest pain to about 4% and atypical angina to about 10%; fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL lowers it to about 9%; and a higher maximum heart rate lowers it steadily, from about 23% at 118 to about 15% at 175 beats per minute.

sentences.label: Raising the risk
sentences.text: Each extra vessel coloured by fluoroscopy adds about the same, from about 18% at 0 to about 86% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher; a flat rather than upsloping ST segment raises it to about 56%, a reversible defect on the thallium scan to about 38% and chest pain brought on by exercise to about 35%; higher cholesterol raises it steadily, from about 11% at 193 mg/dL to about 33% at 308 mg/dL, and higher resting blood pressure steadily, from about 12% at 110 mm Hg to about 30% at 155 mm Hg.
Through this sum alone, a resting ECG other than normal raises it from about 18% to about 24%; the resting ECG also acts through the ST depression signal (below).

sentences.label: Rare results
sentences.text: Some rarer results also count (the model has little data on this, n = 2 to 17): a thallium result coded 4 raises the risk to about 79%, a fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers it to about 9%, and a downsloping ST segment leaves it at about 19%.

This part reads ST depression on exercise and the resting ECG, and acts on 105 of 242 training patients, 66 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is about 76% without it and about 91% with it.
Through it, more ST depression adds nothing until about 0.5 mm, then raises the predicted risk steadily: for a typical patient from about 16% at 0 mm to about 60% at 2.8 mm.
ST depression counts more with a normal resting ECG, nothing until about 0.5 mm and then steadily, from about 16% to about 60%, against about 21% to about 48% with any other resting ECG.
Through it, a resting ECG other than normal lowers a typical patient's risk from about 18% to about 16%.
This part acts on 148 of 242 training patients, 81 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is about 91% without it and about 92% with it.
Through it, age adds nothing until about 53 years, then raises the risk steadily, for a typical patient from about 18% at 42 to about 19% at 66 years.

lead.text: For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms and median test results) the model predicts a risk of heart disease of about 18%; it adds up most of its inputs independently, and two parts add to that sum: a signal from ST depression on exercise and the resting ECG that acts on 105 of 242 training patients, and an age term that acts on 148.

parts.name: heart_disease_logit
parts.original_hypothesis: Root: p = sigmoid(z), z = -0.536 + LINEAR CORE + 0.049*ischaemia_chain[204] + 0.216*ischaemia_chain[290] + 0.082*age_hinge. LINEAR CORE (17 direct input->output edges, z-scored inputs): ca +1.485, sex:0 -1.042, slope:1 -0.873, chol +0.551, cp:1 -0.494, trestbps +0.483, thal:3 -0.471, cp:3 -0.442, slope:3 -0.434, exang:1 +0.423, thal:6 -0.421, cp:4 +0.354, fbs:0 +0.274, thalach -0.213, restecg:0 -0.188, thal:4 +0.172, thal:7 +0.025. Seven inputs are unconnected (sex:1, cp:2, fbs:1, restecg:1, restecg:2, exang:0, slope:2; zero-effect entries of this root). Oldpeak and age have no direct edge and act only through the children; restecg:0 acts both directly and through the ischaemia chain (split into restecg:0_a direct and restecg:0_b). COMPOSITION: additive. The two children are read out additively into z: ischaemia_chain (two exits: a one-sided ST-depression score opened earlier by a normal resting ECG, and a steeper second stage of the same score) and age_hinge (an age term that starts just below the median age). Together the chain gives oldpeak a hinge-shaped effect: about 0.12 logit per SD between its two thresholds and about 1.10 per SD above the second (z-oldpeak -0.39 with a normal ECG, +0.40 otherwise). EVIDENCE (train, n=242): full model AUC 0.9376, acc 0.888 (compute_performance). Linear core alone AUC 0.9317; logit SD 3.22 (core) vs 0.80 (nonlinear readouts). Removing the whole chain (204 with downstream) gives 0.9317; readout-only ablations: 204 0.9380, 290 0.9341, age 0.9371. All ReLUs as identities 0.9304; one least-squares linear fit of all nonlinear readouts on restecg:0, oldpeak and age gives 0.9355 (R2 0.88); an L2 logistic regression on all 26 inputs gives 0.9355. Mean |SHAP| (kernel, all 242 train rows): ca 0.141, sex:0 0.104, slope:1 0.099, oldpeak 0.060, thal:3 0.054, exang:1 0.045, chol 0.044, cp:3 0.043, cp:4 0.040, trestbps 0.040. Interpretation: close to logistic regression plus one ST-depression correction that switches on above a threshold (lower for patients with a normal resting ECG) and a small age term above median age. Counter-directional signs reported, not explained: a normal resting ECG lowers the oldpeak threshold inside the chain (raising risk), fbs:0 (normal fasting sugar) +0.27 directly, thal:7 (reversible defect) only +0.025. Compared with the 10-seed heart-s5 record (generation 37, key 9330: ischaemia gate -> resting-BP gate -> age term) and its cluster-1 sibling: the same ischaemia gate on oldpeak and restecg:0, but here the second stage is a steeper copy of the score (no resting-BP offset) and the age term is a free-standing hinge (not switched off by the chain).

parts.name: ischaemia_chain
parts.original_hypothesis: Ischaemia chain (raises risk with ST depression, in two stages). 204 = ReLU(0.245 + 2.501*oldpeak + 0.980*restecg:0); 3487 = ReLU(0.940*204 - 0.002) (a near-copy of 204); 290 = ReLU(-0.468 + 1.008*204 + 0.862*3487) = ReLU(1.818*204 - 0.470) whenever 204 > 0.0023. Readouts: logit += 0.049*204 + 0.216*290. Hypothesis: an ST-depression score that opens above an oldpeak threshold set by the resting ECG (z-oldpeak -0.49 with a normal ECG, +0.29 otherwise) and then a second, much steeper stage once the score passes 0.259 (z-oldpeak -0.39 with a normal ECG, +0.40 otherwise). Net effect on the logit: about 0.12 per SD of oldpeak between the two thresholds and about 1.10 per SD above the second, i.e. a hinge in oldpeak whose position moves about 0.78 SD lower with a normal resting ECG. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): 204 active for 105/242 (58 of 121 with a normal ECG, 47 of 121 without); 290 active for 96/242; disease rate 66% when 290 is active vs 30% when not; corr(204, oldpeak) 0.91. Sensitivities (mean |d exit/d entry|): 290: oldpeak 1.82, restecg:0 0.71; 204: oldpeak 1.09, restecg:0 0.43. Ablation: removing 204 with its downstream (the whole chain) lowers train AUC 0.9376 -> 0.9317, the linear-core level; removing the steepener readout (290) alone 0.9341; removing 204's own readout 0.9380 (no loss). An affine replacement of 290 on 204 fits almost perfectly (R2 0.998, AUC 0.9376): the steepening is a hinge that the data barely probe on its flat side. Supported. Oldpeak has no direct edge and acts only here. Counter-intuitive sign reported, not explained: a normal resting ECG (restecg:0) lowers the oldpeak threshold (raising risk) inside the chain, partly offset by its direct -0.188 edge.

parts.name: age_hinge
parts.original_hypothesis: Age hinge (raises risk with age above a threshold, small). 1987 = ReLU(0.191 + 0.872*age), read out +0.082. Hypothesis: age's only route to the output; nothing below z-age -0.22 (just under the median age), then +0.072 logit per SD of age. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): active for 148/242; disease rate 55% when active vs 28% when not; line plot correlation 0.90; mean |sensitivity| 0.53. Removing it lowers train AUC 0.9376 -> 0.9371; an affine replacement (R2 0.80) gives 0.9376. Supported, near-negligible.

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points

ann_27.text: This part acts on 105 of 242 training patients (43%).
For a typical patient it acts on, it raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 76% without this part to about 91% with it (on the training data only).
In the training data, 66 of these 105 patients had heart disease.

A higher ST depression on exercise clearly raises the predicted risk of heart disease, and even more so if the resting ECG is normal (with nothing until about 0.5 mm, then steadily for patients with a normal resting ECG): for a typical patient, ST depression on exercise going from 0.0 mm to 2.8 mm moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 16% to about 60% if the resting ECG is normal, and from about 21% to about 48% if resting ECG is something other than a normal resting ECG.

Through this part, the model treats a higher ST depression on exercise as raising the predicted risk of heart disease with nothing until about 0.5 mm, then steadily: for a typical patient, it goes from about 16% at 0.0 mm to about 60% at 2.8 mm (on the training data only).

Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a slightly lower predicted risk of heart disease if resting ECG is something other than a normal resting ECG (about 16%) than if the resting ECG is normal (about 18%) (on the training data only).

ann_28.text: This part acts on 148 of 242 training patients (61%).
For a typical patient it acts on, it slightly raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 91% without this part to about 92% with it (on the training data only).
In the training data, 81 of these 148 patients had heart disease.

Through this part, age only slightly adds to the predicted risk of heart disease once it rises above about 53 years: for a typical such patient, going from 29 years to 68 years moves it from about 18% to about 20% (on the training data only).

Through this part, the model treats a higher age as slightly raising the predicted risk of heart disease with nothing until about 53 years, then steadily: for a typical patient, it goes from about 18% at 42 years to about 19% at 66 years (on the training data only).

ann_29.text: The model treats a higher number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily, each extra vessel adding about the same: for a typical patient, it goes from about 18% at 0 vessels to about 86% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher (on the training data only).

For a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if thallium stress test result coded 4 (meaning not recorded) applies (about 79%) than if the thallium scan is normal (about 18%) (on the training data only). The model has little data on this: only 2 training patients (thallium stress test result coded 4 (meaning not recorded)).

The model treats a higher ST depression on exercise as raising the predicted risk of heart disease with nothing until about 0.5 mm, then steadily: for a typical patient, it goes from about 16% at 0.0 mm to about 60% at 2.8 mm (on the training data only).

For a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if the ST segment is flat at peak exercise (about 56%) than if the ST segment slopes up at peak exercise (about 18%) (on the training data only).

The model treats a higher serum cholesterol as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily: for a typical patient, it goes from about 11% at 193 mg/dL (5.0 mmol/L) to about 33% at 308 mg/dL (8.0 mmol/L) (on the training data only).

For a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if the thallium scan shows a reversible defect (about 38%) than if the thallium scan is normal (about 18%) (on the training data only).

Other effects: a higher resting blood pressure raises it steadily; chest pain brought on by exercise (rather than no chest pain on exercise) raises it; typical angina (rather than no chest pain (asymptomatic)) lowers it; female (rather than male) lowers it; non-anginal chest pain (rather than no chest pain (asymptomatic)) lowers it; fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL (rather than fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less) lowers it; a fixed defect on the thallium scan (rather than a normal thallium scan) lowers it; a higher maximum heart rate lowers it steadily; and 2 still smaller effects listed in the evidence table (on the training data only). The model has little data on some of these: only 15 training patients (a fixed defect on the thallium scan).

Smaller effects, each changing the predicted value only slightly: a higher age raises it with nothing until about 53 years, then steadily; a downsloping ST segment (rather than an upsloping ST segment) raises it (on the training data only). The model has little data on some of these: only 17 training patients (a downsloping ST segment).
